questions.markdown:
A Ge diode carries a current of 55 mA when it is forward biased with 0.3 V at 27°C. If the temperature is increased by 5°C, determine the following:

i) Change in diode current.

ii) The forward voltage to maintain the same diode current of 55 mA.
For the circuit shown below in figure Q1B, determine the value of $V_{GS}$ required to get $V_{DS}=2.8\,\text{V}$, if $\mu_n C_{ox}=250\,\mu\text{A}/\text{V}^2$ and $V_{Th}=0.5\,\text{V}$.

questions.markdown: Consider the half wave rectifier shown in figure Q1C. Explain the operation of the rectifier during positive and negative half cycle. Also, draw waveform of output voltage and output current across the load resistor. Derive the equation of RMS load current.

questions.markdown: A full wave rectifier supplying a resistive load is fed from a transformer having turns ratio of 5:1. The primary voltage of the transformer is 150 V at 50 Hz. If a capacitor filter is connected across the load, the average load current is 500 mA. Determine the rating of capacitor to maintain the ripple factor less than 0.02.

For the Zener voltage regulator circuit shown in figure Q2B, $R_S=100\,\Omega$, $V_Z=10\,\text{V}$, $P_{ZM}=1\,\text{W}$, $P_{ZK}=200\,\text{mW}$ and $R_L=1\,\text{k}\Omega$. Determine the range of values of $V_S$ that will maintain Zener diode in the breakdown region. Also, compute the range of potential difference between cathode and anode terminals of the Zener diode.

diagrams.caption: Figure Q2B: Zener voltage regulator circuit with source $V_S$, series resistor $R_S$, Zener diode $V_Z$, and load resistor $R_L$. (original source region)

questions.markdown: Explain the common-mode gain and differential-mode gain of an Op-Amp and provide their expressions in terms of the voltages at the inverting and non-inverting inputs. An Op-Amp has a common mode gain of 100 and CMRR of 60 dB. If non-inverting input voltage is 140 $\mu$V and inverting input voltage is 120 $\mu$V, calculate the output voltage of OPAMP.

Implement the following output function using inverting op-amps. Choose feedback resistance as $R_f=10\,\text{k}\Omega$.

$$
V_o=5V_1-V_2-3V_3+2V_4
$$

A 7-bit even parity Hamming code is used to encode a given 4-bit data, d. The codeword received at the receiver is "1111110". Decode the codeword to determine the transmitted data d, assuming a single error occurred.

Implement the following logical function using a 4:1 MUX

$$
F(x,y,z)=\sum m(2,4,5,7).
$$

Simplify the following logical expression using K-Map and implement using only NAND gates:

$$
F(A,B,C,D)=\sum m(0,4,6,12)+\sum d(8,14)
$$
Realize a 3-bit down counter using positive edge triggered JK flip flops. Draw the timing diagram for the same.

Implement a 4-bit Serial-In Parallel-Out (SIPO) Shift Register. Show the flip-flops and indicate the input $D_n$, clock signal, and output, $Q_n$ for each flip-flop. Write a table which shows the contents of all registers after each clock pulse while shifting operation is done. The table must show all entries till the data is shifted out completely. Assume 4-bit data as 1010 and data is entered starting from MSB.

A 200 W, 90 kHz carrier is amplitude modulated to a depth of 65% by a modulating signal of 5 kHz frequency. Given $R_L=1\,\text{k}\Omega$. Determine the:

i) Total power transmitted.

ii) Power transmitted in sideband frequencies.

iii) Bandwidth of transmitted signal.

iv) Plot the frequency spectrum of the resulting AM wave.
Draw the block diagram of analog communication system. Explain the operation of each block.
For given binary data 11011010, sketch the ASK, FSK and PSK signals.
